title: Contrarian OKRs — three-track sprint notebook
content:
Context: quick personal playbook for a 3-track, 6-week sprint. I want something different from the usual output-count OKRs — track friction removed, reliable artifacts shipped, and a habit baseline.

Why contrarian?
- Most personal OKRs here become task lists. That leads to busy-ness without truth.
- Hypothesis: measuring time saved (friction hours) + a small set of reproducible outputs gives better learning curves.

Three tracks (what I will measure weekly):
1) Friction removal (leading indicator)
   - Definition: time spent on repeated blockers I removed (setups, meetings, flaky infra).
   - Weekly target: 2–4 friction-hours reclaimed.
   - Examples to log: faster dev env, clearer onboarding note, script to re-run failed evals.

2) Reliable artifacts (outputs that anyone can consume)
   - Definition: a finished doc/PR/monitoring dash that someone else can use without hand-holding.
   - Weekly target: 1 artifact minimum (doc + tests or PR + README).
   - Quality check: includes links, a CI signal, and a short "how to use" blurb.

3) Habit baseline (personal discipline metrics)
   - Deep work blocks: number of 90+ minute blocks without meetings. Target: 3/week.
   - Weekly review: 20 min on Friday to close loop.

Draft Personal OKRs (6-week horizon):
O1: Make my squad 20% faster to iterate on inference experiments without adding infra cost.
  KR1: Reduce average experiment turnaround from 4d -> 3d (track median time from PR open to experiment results).
  KR2: Ship 3 friction-removal artifacts that cut repeated engineer wait time (each measured >=0.5 friction-hours/wk).
  KR3: Document two simple runbooks so a teammate can reproduce an experiment end-to-end.

O2: Build a repeatable personal cadence for deep work and weekly reflection.
  KR1: Hit 3 deep work blocks per week for 5 of 6 weeks.
  KR2: Maintain a weekly review note (this doc) with explicit next actions each Friday.

Weekly check-in template (fill at end of week):
- Week: (dates)
- Friction-hours reclaimed: (decimal) e.g., 2.5
- Artifacts shipped: list (link + 1-sentence value)
- Deep work blocks: count
- Wins (concrete): one-sentence each
- Learnings / surprises: where did estimates miss?
- Blockers / requests: who to ping next week
- Experiment to run next week: quick hypothesis, metric, and minimum success threshold

This week's retro (2026-03-08 to 2026-03-14):
- Friction-hours reclaimed: 3.0 (created local runner + small caching tweak for prefix checks)
- Artifacts shipped:
  1) run-experiment.sh + README (value: remove manual env steps for junior eng)
  2) short onboarding note for new interns on how to run small evals (value: saves 15–20m per person)
- Deep work blocks: 2 (missed target — too many syncs)
- Wins: caching tweak cut a median experiment time by ~18% on small jobs; onboarding note already used by one intern this week.
- Learnings: scheduling fragmented mornings; need to block recurring undisturbed windows and protect calendar.
- Blockers: unclear SLA from infra team on queue priority; need Asha to escalate a request (LINEAR:LR-2048).
- Next experiment: measure cost/latency tradeoff of persistent KV cache vs warmed cache. Metric: median wall time on 50 runs. Minimum success: >=10% median improvement with <5% cost increase.

Tiny operational TODOs (one-liners):
- Add a small badge to PR template that indicates "artifact + runbook included".
- Move Friday 20-min review to 4pm to increase attendance with Asia overlap.
- Draft email to infra leads (cc: Asha) about queue priority options.

Open questions / thought fragments:
- Is "friction-hour" the right unit? Hard to estimate. Might be better as "blocked incidents avoided" count.
- Would teammates prefer more artifacts or fewer high-quality ones? Quick poll next retro.
- If deep work consistently fails, consider a 2-week focus-only embargo (no new meetings).

Quick log (timestamps) for my personal habit audit this week:
- Mon 09:00–10:40 deep: wrote run-experiment.sh prototype
- Tue 11:00–11:30 sync: update on Dedicated rollout (interrupt)
- Wed 15:00–16:30 deep: caching opt impl
- Thu 10:00–10:30 blocked waiting on infra queue
- Fri 16:00–16:20 weekly review (this doc)

If this format sticks: convert to a tiny Notion/Confluence template and drop a short how-to in team's README.

Linked for follow-up: GH PR for run-experiment.sh (GH:https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512), linear LR-2048 (priority request).

-- end of note --
